correctness.rationale: All quantifiers specify n>=2 and iid atomless common endpoints. The 2rs bridging probability yields the exact beta-integral formula, and a one-dimensional beta integration plus a uniform-integrable exponential comparison gives the Euler-constant correction. Compact corner-binomial processes converge jointly to independent PPPs; a two-sided truncation estimate controls pair counts from small and large corner coordinates. Campbell integration gives the infinite mean, and a protected-midpoint-bridge argument bounds graph diameter by three with probability 1-o(1). An independent exhaustive exact-rational enumeration of all 11,463 matchings for n=2 through 6 established 11,478 finite assertions. Finite checks supplement, but do not substitute for, the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Graph distance three measures unavoidable two-hop communication failure in a high-density natural interval network; graph diameter is already often known, but the multiplicity of worst-distance pairs is not deducible from that event. The exact expected count grows as log n while the typical count is tight, with an almost surely finite limit of infinite mean. This motivated and structurally explained nonuniform-integrability transition is mathematically informative beyond direct reformulation of classic universal-interval probabilities.
